name: iac-security-review
description: Use when reviewing Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Dockerfile or CI pipeline changes for security problems. Produces a findings list with file:line evidence and a severity per finding. Read-only.
title: IaC security review
goal: Read the change and report security problems with evidence. Never apply, plan or deploy anything.
steps: Run `python3 {{skill_dir}}/scripts/changed_iac.py <base>` (the base branch, for example origin/main). It lists the changed files grouped as terraform, helm, dockerfile, ci and kubernetes. Exit code 3 means nothing relevant changed; say so and stop.
Read each changed file in full, then the files it references (modules, values, base images).
Terraform: public ingress on non-HTTP ports, `*` in IAM actions or resources, unencrypted storage, public buckets, secrets in variables or defaults.
Kubernetes/Helm: privileged or root containers, hostPath/hostNetwork, missing limits, `latest` tags, secrets in env or ConfigMaps, wildcard RBAC.
Dockerfile: unpinned base image, running as root, secrets in ARG/ENV/layers, `curl | sh`.
CI: untrusted input in shell steps, long-lived credentials instead of OIDC, third-party actions not pinned to a commit.
If tfsec, checkov, trivy or kube-linter are installed, run them read-only and merge the results. If not, say so; do not install anything.
Only report what you read. Mark anything inferred as "unverified".
output: One table: severity | file:line | problem | evidence (quoted line) | fix. End with "Not checked:" listing what you could not see.
gotchas: A default value in a variable file is still a finding if it opens access.
A finding in code that the change removes is not a finding.
The script only lists files. It does not judge them; read each one yourself.
